A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same DisWM study, including Supplementary Material A–D. Text comparison and rendered-page inspection support reliable comparison of the main text, appendices, equations, tables and figures.

before.justification: v2 reports original reinforcement-learning experiments, ablations and qualitative analyses in Section 4, plus DMC and DrawerWorld results in Supplementary Tables A–B.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results, including the learning curves, ablations and supplementary benchmark outcomes.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same action-free representation pretraining, latent distillation, disentangled world-model adaptation and actor–critic learning procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same DMC source and target tasks, MuJoCo Pusher and DrawerWorld scenarios, including supplementary Humanoid Walk evaluation and the same color and texture variations.

E2.justification: Figure 4 retains DreamerV2, DV2 Finetune, APV, TED and CURL. Table A retains DreamerV3, TD-MPC2 and ContextWM; Table B retains TD-MPC2 and ContextWM. The runtime comparators in Table C also match.

E3.justification: The reported DMC training budget, image preprocessing, color and texture switching procedures, evaluation metrics and model configurations are unchanged. Supplementary analyses retain their settings, including 200 clips of length 50 for the t-SNE visualization.

E4.justification: Both retain the same component ablations, distillation/disentanglement sensitivity tests, source-video comparisons, latent-dimension analysis and qualitative visualizations in Figures 5–8, I and J.

E5.justification: The shaded learning-curve bands and ± reporting in Tables A–B are unchanged. Neither version adds or revises run counts, seeds, uncertainty definitions or significance tests.

E6.justification: The plotted findings and supplementary numerical results match. For example, Table A retains DisWM's 817 ± 59 episode return for Reacher Easy to Cheetah Run, and Table B retains 77 ± 6% success on DrawerClose. Table C's runtime and parameter values also match.

T1.justification: The POMDP formulation and mathematical definitions and objectives in Equations (1)–(9), including supplementary behavior learning, are unchanged. No assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about transferring disentanglement knowledge from distracting videos, improving sample efficiency and handling environmental variations.

C2.justification: Interpretations of distillation, disentanglement, hyperparameter sensitivity and online sample diversity are unchanged. Section 6 retains the limitation concerning complex environments and time-varying background distractions.

D1.justification: Both provide the same project link, video-collection description, GPU memory and training-time estimates, implementation details and Table D hyperparameters. No reproducibility information is added or removed.

R1.justification: The same 48 references and related-work discussion are retained, with unchanged positioning relative to visual model-based RL, representation learning and transfer from videos.

P1.justification: The arXiv margin stamp changes from v2, 28 August 2025, to v3, 4 April 2026. The prose, terminology, headings and main-text/supplementary organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–8 and I–J, Tables 1 and A–D, and Algorithm 1 retain their designs, captions and placements. Rendered inspection shows the same axes, legends and page layout; negligible glyph-position differences do not constitute a layout revision.

improvement.justification: v3 preserves the same scientific content, experimental evidence, explanations, reproducibility information and limitations, including the appendices. The updated version/date stamp and negligible typesetting differences have no meaningful effect on overall paper quality.
